approachQuestion.prompt:
Read Escaped Fields

A message contains lowercase ASCII letters, vertical bars (|), and backslashes (\). An unescaped | ends the current field. A backslash escapes exactly the next character, which is copied literally into the field, even if it is | or another backslash. A final backslash with no next character makes the whole message invalid. Return the decoded fields as flat strings, or null if invalid. Empty fields are preserved.

Example 1: message characters=[a,BACKSLASH,|,b,|,c] → ["a|b","c"].
Example 2: message characters=[|,|] → ["","",""]; message characters=[] → [""].
Example 3: message characters=[a,BACKSLASH] → null.
Example 4: message characters=[BACKSLASH,BACKSLASH,|,a] → [one-backslash string,"a"].

Constraints:
0 ≤ n=message.length ≤ 200,000. Only a–z, | and backslash occur.
Do not modify message. Return [""] for an empty message.
Examples use character lists to make backslashes unambiguous: BACKSLASH denotes one actual backslash character.
constraints: 0 ≤ n=message.length ≤ 200,000. Only a–z, | and backslash occur.
Do not modify message. Return [""] for an empty message.
Examples use character lists to make backslashes unambiguous: BACKSLASH denotes one actual backslash character.

options.text: Scan left to right with an escape flag and a mutable current-field buffer. If escaped, append the current character literally and clear the flag; otherwise a backslash sets the flag, a bar emits the field, and a letter appends. At the end reject a set escape flag; otherwise emit the final field.
options.feedback: The escape flag gives the previous backslash exactly one-character scope. It distinguishes literal separators from field boundaries and catches a dangling escape.

options.text: Copy all message characters into a helper array, then run the same escape-state parser on that copy using a field buffer and output list.
options.feedback: This follows the grammar correctly, but the full input copy is avoidable: scanning original characters by index gives the same parser state.

options.text: Split the original message at every bar, then remove escape backslashes separately within each field. Reject a trailing escape within a split field.
options.feedback: An escaped bar is data, not a separator. Example 1 must keep a|b in a single field; splitting first destroys that boundary information.

options.text: Treat a bar as escaped exactly when its immediately previous original character is a backslash, regardless of earlier backslashes. Otherwise use the grammar’s backslash decoding and reject a dangling escape.
options.feedback: An escaped backslash does not itself escape the bar after it. For [BACKSLASH,BACKSLASH,|,a], the two backslashes form a literal backslash and the bar is an actual separator, despite its immediate predecessor.

feedback.reason: An escape flag is parser state: an escaped backslash is literal and does not automatically escape the following separator.
details: Use an escape flag and a mutable field buffer. An escaped character is always literal. Otherwise a backslash arms the flag and a bar emits the field. After the scan, reject an armed flag or emit the final field.

An escape flag is parser state: an escaped backslash is literal and does not automatically escape the following separator. A bare separator closes the current field, including an empty field. A final armed escape flag signals an invalid message rather than a silently accepted suffix.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Track One-Character Escape State”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the original length. Indexed reads and flag updates cost constant time. Buffer append and output-list append have amortized constant cost, including resizing copies. Emitting a field copies its buffer into a new flat string and clears that buffer; sum all such copy costs. Exclude input and the returned list/strings for a successful parse. Include the separate field buffer, helpers and stack; invalid parses may also retain partial output until returning null. No recursion or hashing. Use a bound valid for n=0.
constraints: 0 ≤ n=message.length ≤ 200,000. Only a–z, | and backslash occur.
Do not modify message. Return [""] for an empty message.
Examples use character lists to make backslashes unambiguous: BACKSLASH denotes one actual backslash character.

feedback.reason: Scan characters once and include the separately retained field buffer.
details: The parser visits each input character once. Total decoded field lengths and number of emitted fields are at most linear in n+1, so all amortized appends and field copies are linear in total. A single unseparated field can grow the separate buffer to n characters. An invalid parse can retain partial output, also bounded by n+1.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: One scan plus a linear total of copied characters and fields gives these tight worst-case bounds.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The mutable field buffer is a separate helper, and may contain the whole message.
The option “O((n + 1)²) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: The buffer is mutable and emitted fields are disjoint; earlier output is not recopied each step.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(n² + 1) auxiliary space.”: Only a linear total of decoded characters and field records is stored.
